clue.text: His garden's prepared with gap for yucca (13, two words)

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: Someone clears a gap in their garden bed ready to plant a yucca.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish dagger is a common name for several yucca species, from their stiff sword-like leaves.

clue.text: Old Harry, eccentric, that may reveal winning number (11, two words)

parts.note: Old Harry and Old Scratch are both nicknames for the Devil
a card is an amusingly odd person

explanation.surface: An eccentric old fellow called Harry seems to be the man who might reveal the lottery winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Harry reads like a person, but it is one of the Devil's nicknames, as is Old Scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch card is a lottery ticket whose coating is rubbed off to show whether a prize has been won.

clue.text: Video that trails concert, introducing orchestra's leader

indicators.note: introducing means the concert word leads in and the next letter follows it

parts.note: a Prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

indicators.note: the leader of a group is the one at its front, so keep the opening letter

explanation.surface: A trailer for a concert opens with the orchestra's lead violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trails' here means advertises in advance, as a film trailer does, not lags behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional film, typically a music clip, made to advertise something forthcoming.

clue.text: African people turned up round edge of equator

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the result is read from bottom to top
round means the verb's letters go around the single letter

parts.note: spun is a past tense meaning turned

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

explanation.surface: A tribe somewhere on the equator is said to have got its back up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nupe are an ethnic group of central Nigeria, so the plural names members of that people.

clue.text: Making awkward progress dropping bling — it's not real

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of part of the word, the slang word for jewellery

parts.note: to shamble is to walk clumsily
slang for flashy jewellery, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling along without their flashy jewellery looks a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a pretence or fake, something passed off as genuine.

clue.text: Mother and children lacking nothing on which games are played

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: lacking means the children's word goes without one of its letters

parts.note: a brood is a family of young

explanation.surface: A mother and her children have nothing to play games on.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one O from the word for children before adding it after the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Dambrod is a Scots word for a draughtboard, the board used for draughts (checkers).

clue.text: Franco-US artist supplied by fellow serving drinks (not his first)

indicators.note: not his first means the opening letter of the drink-server's word is removed

parts.note: a man who serves at a bar

explanation.surface: An artist is kept in drinks by a bartender.
explanation.definitionFit: Arman was a French-born American sculptor and painter known for his accumulations of everyday objects.

clue.text: What thugs used on piercing wretched target

indicators.note: piercing means the small word is driven into the middle of the jumbled one
something wretched is in a sorry state, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: Chambers allows O as an abbreviation for on

explanation.surface: Thugs stab some poor victim.
explanation.walkthrough: O standing for 'on' is unusual, but Chambers lists it.
explanation.definitionFit: A garotte is a cord or wire for strangling, a weapon of street robbers in Victorian times.

clue.text: Raptor having a catch under wing

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means the following pieces sit below the first

parts.note: an el (or ell) is a wing extension of a building

explanation.surface: A bird of prey grips its catch under one wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' looks like the bird's, but it is the architectural sense, an extension of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An elanet is a kite of the genus Elanus, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Kinship

parts.note: surface reading: the plain dictionary meaning, being of the same family
setter's reading: this is the puzzle's competition entry, which solvers were invited to clue themselves, so no wordplay is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was Azed's clue-writing competition word: the printed clue is only the definition, and solvers had to supply their own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being related means being connected by blood or marriage, which is what kinship describes.

clue.text: Burslem product — squat, mind

parts.note: ware is an old verb for beware, as in mind out

explanation.surface: A factory in Burslem is told to squat and look out.
explanation.walkthrough: Burslem is one of the Staffordshire Potteries towns, home of English ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: Crouchware is an early salt-glazed stoneware made in Burslem, an example of the town's pottery.

clue.text: Simple optical device we learnt after adjusting section (9, two words)

indicators.note: after places the reworked letters ahead of the single letter that follows them
adjusting means altering, so these letters are moved into another order

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: In physics class we learned about a simple lens after rearranging part of the syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: A water lens is a magnifier made from a drop or vessel of water, about the simplest lens there is.

clue.text: Jock's husky, no good when fed nothing

indicators.note: when fed means something is put inside the poor-quality word

parts.note: ropy is British slang for poor or shoddy

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's sled dog is useless unless it gets nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the dog, but it means hoarse; Jock marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roopy is Scots for hoarse, as husky can describe a rough, croaky voice.

clue.text: Some cows'll follow you wanting nothing — like a rash?

indicators.note: follow means the cattle word comes after the other piece
wanting means lacking, so the word for you goes without a letter

parts.note: ky (also kye) is a Scots plural for cows; the 'll just means will

explanation.surface: A herd of cattle trails behind someone who seems to have come out in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuky is a dialect word for itchy, which is how a rash makes the skin feel.

clue.text: Former commander at sea, one having pain trapping his foreign counterpart

indicators.note: trapping means holding the counterpart's title inside the word for pain

parts.note: mal is an illness or ailment, as in mal de mer
mir is a variant of emir, a Muslim commander or ruler

explanation.surface: An old naval officer is in pain, holding his opposite number from a foreign fleet prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The admiral and the emir share an origin, the Arabic amir, which makes the foreign counterpart apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammiral is an obsolete spelling of admiral, a naval officer of top rank.

clue.text: Eucalypt hosting European member of Rosaceae

indicators.note: a host holds a guest, so the tree's word goes around the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A gum tree has a European rose-family plant growing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Geum, or avens, is a genus of perennials in the rose family, Rosaceae.

clue.text: Monkey? One accepted in place of clue

indicators.note: taken in place of means one item swaps out another inside the definition word

parts.note: the definition word itself is reused for the wordplay
a key is something that leads to the solution of a problem

explanation.surface: A question about a monkey, with the setter offering a single word instead of a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay works on the definition word itself, swapping its second half for a single letter; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: The mona is a West African guenon, a species of monkey.

clue.text: Beside river in spate? Less than half — but it's fairly high

parts.note: to can mean beside, as in cheek to cheek
a second route: the answer is the first three of the seven letters of a word for a river in spate

explanation.surface: A river in flood is only half as high as a nearby hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings agree: TO + R, and the opening three letters of TORRENT, a river in spate, under half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, as on Dartmoor, high ground but not a mountain.

clue.text: What can be rendered spicier when one goes for heart of pimento?

definitions.text: What can be rendered spicier when one goes for heart of pimento?

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters are reworked
goes for means one letter leaves and another takes its place

parts.note: the central letter of the seven-letter pimento

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what dishes could be livened up by swapping in the core of a pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap one I in the comparative for the central letter of pimento, then rearrange; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking instructions are what can be adjusted to make food hotter, for instance by adding pimento.

clue.text: Bird fed in groups of three

parts.note: fed as in ate a meal

explanation.surface: Seabirds were fed in threes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ternate describes leaves or parts arranged in threes, from Latin terni, three each.

clue.text: Typical of theologian, allowing some obscurity

parts.note: tho is a short form of though, meaning allowing that

explanation.surface: A theologian's writing is typically somewhat obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomist means following Thomas Aquinas, the medieval theologian whose system is Thomism.

clue.text: Women grasped in cold dance, anything but tender

parts.note: C abbreviates cold, as on taps

indicators.note: grasped in means held inside the dance word

parts.note: a hey is a country dance

explanation.surface: Women are held in a chilly dance, anything but tenderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewy food is tough and needs a lot of chewing, the opposite of tender meat.

clue.text: Bairns fidget so, and relish misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving means not keeping proper order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Scottish children wriggle and enjoy being naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairns are Scottish children, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hirsle is Scots for to shuffle or wriggle along, as fidgeting children do.

clue.text: Learner lacking in courage making pass

indicators.note: lacking in means the word for courage goes without the learner's letter

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A timid learner driver plucks up nerve to overtake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like overtaking or a test result, but it is a lunge in fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: A botte is a pass or thrust in fencing, from the French term.

clue.text: Diary anyone may read left in the loo

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for lavatory

parts.note: bog is British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: Someone's private diary, left in the toilet, is open to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A blog is an online journal published for public reading, unlike a private diary.

clue.text: Italian cook's starter, whipped dolce, straight from the freezer?

indicators.note: whipped like cream, the dessert word is beaten into a new order
a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: Italian for a dessert, taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian chef serves a whipped dessert straight out of the freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken straight from the freezer is extremely chilled, frozen through.

clue.text: Councillor admits age rising, calling for social worker

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the abbreviation goes around the other piece
in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards

explanation.surface: An ageing councillor admits needing help from social services.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone who is ill or disabled, often as paid social care.

clue.text: Something that accompanies memento, a folly

parts.note: memento mori, the Latin reminder of death

explanation.surface: A souvenir comes with something foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Moria is an old word, from Greek, for foolishness or a form of mental weakness.

clue.text: Tip I've removed from salad plant

indicators.note: removed from means taking the contraction out of the plant's name

explanation.surface: A cook has trimmed the tip off a salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of something is its tip or extremity.

clue.text: Defenceless and somehow protecting king, English

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the others
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A chess king left with no defenders somehow, despite English protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked can mean exposed and unprotected, as in a naked flame or naked aggression.

clue.text: Cold wind returning, accounting for young pampas creature

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for wind is read backwards

parts.note: air is a breeze, or a wind in music

explanation.surface: A cold wind blowing back explains why a young animal on the plains shivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cria is a baby llama or alpaca, animals of the South American Andes and grasslands.

clue.text: Secluded spot, acceptable after retiring certainly

indicators.note: after places the word for certainly following the turned piece
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the acceptable word is read in reverse

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in that's not on
OK as a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A shy person agrees to a quiet spot.
explanation.walkthrough: OK seems to be 'acceptable', but here acceptable is ON, and OK is 'certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or recess, out of the way.

clue.text: Disciple holds one up in sanctum sanctorum

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the disciple word is read from bottom to top
holds means the turned disciple word goes around the number

parts.note: a disciple is a spiritual son

explanation.surface: A follower raises one hand in the holy of holies.
explanation.definitionFit: The naos is the inner chamber of a Greek temple housing the cult image, its holiest part.

clue.text: Endlessly ambitious, one may inhibit clots

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A go-getter who can stop idiots in their tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clots' looks like fools, but it means blood clots.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin thins the blood and is taken to reduce the risk of thrombosis.

clue.text: Trouble cutting off furlong round Grand Canyon

indicators.note: round means the shortened word wraps around the thousand
cutting off means trimming away, so the abbreviation leaves the word for trouble

parts.note: grief means trouble, as in giving someone grief
a grand is a thousand, K

explanation.surface: Some trouble with a measuring chain in the Grand Canyon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand Canyon' looks like a place name, but Grand is K and Canyon is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grike is a deep fissure in limestone pavement, a canyon in miniature.

clue.text: Garnets I found among stones he's fashioned

indicators.note: found among means sitting inside the other letters
fashioned means shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller finds some garnets in among the stones they have cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessonite is a cinnamon-coloured variety of grossular garnet.

clue.text: Creeping snail died, swallowed by rats in lonely places (13, two words)

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside the word for rats

parts.note: to rat is to desert, so rats means deserts

indicators.note: creeping suggests slow wandering movement, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A snail crept along and died, eaten by rats in a remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like the animals, but it is the verb: to rat is to desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert islands are uninhabited, isolated places, a byword for solitude.
